newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks steady as traders eye Bank of Spain.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks steady as traders eye Bank of Spain.

text.p: Madrid stocks were little changed at the close, despite falls in foreign markets, as traders took positions ahead of a possible cut in Spanish rates on Tuesday. * General index up 0.09 points, 0.03 percent, to 358.89. * Ibex-35 index gained 4.38 points, 0.11 percent, to 4,097.98. * Telefonica rose five pesetas to 2,390 with 2.2 million shares traded while Repsol was unchanged at 4,095 with volume of just under 332,000 shares.
Five out of ten analysts polled by Reuters forecast the Bank of Spain would cut its key money market rate by a quarter point from 7.25 percent at Tuesday's regular repurchase tender.
"The possibility of precipitated rate cut at tomorrow's auction let our bourse perform better than others, although there is some worry about what will happen afterward," one trader said.
The market was also eyeing the Federal Open Market meeting with the possibility of a U.S. rate hike already discounted.
Trading volume reached more than 30 billion pesetas with favourable interest in the electricity firms, which would benefit from a rate cut. Iberdrola rose 10 pesetas to 1,205.
